title: We Have Everything
subtitle: Your mistakes will be your demise, my friend.

items.text: We Have Everything

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: We were forced to retreat to the village. The brave soldiers who bought us precious time ... we must not forget their names.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Understood, Lieutenant, submit a report later listing the fallen soldiers for Zeno to review.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Their families will be well taken care of.
Bertolt sighs with relief, a faint smile playing on his lips.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: What happened next? What did you discuss with Lilya?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I tried to call for reinforcements. The base responded quickly, but transporting personnel and equipment takes time.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Time. I see. Continue.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I briefed Lilya on the priorities of the mission.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: So, what's our next move? Are we hitting the skies or the slopes?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: You should know what our mission is.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: To rescue the team members, and retrieve some mysterious arcanum documents when we get the chance.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Correct, but I need you to adjust the priorities of these two tasks.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Huh? What's that now?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I mean you need to swap the order of these two tasks—prioritize the arcanum documents first, then rescue any stranded personnel if you happen to get the chance.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You what?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: She was surprised.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: They may already be dead. How long has it been since your device has received a new signal?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: None. Radio silence since the first message.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I don't think the equipment is faulty, but it's been several hours since the last distress call.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Either they're pinned down somewhere and can't move, or they've met their tragic end.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Do the others know about this priority switch?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: No. They don't need to know.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Right as I said that, she punched me in the nose.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: She had to do a little hop.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Tsk!
The officer staggers back, blood trickling from his nose.
She is stronger than she looks.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Liar.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: You really packed a punch with that one, little falcon.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You don't trust them, and you don't trust me.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: No, I trust you and Aleksei.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: And the others?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I trust their loyalty and their fighting ability.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: But they don't need to know any of this. Neither does Aleksei, he'd tell everyone.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: As will I.
She clenches her fist, still wanting to land another blow on her superior's face.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: No sacrifice will be made in vain, Comrade Lilya.
... You youngsters sure mature quickly when you've tangoed with death.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: In other words, your squad had two objectives at the time—to recover the arcanum documents and rescue the relevant team members.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Correct. This mission came directly from the admiral's office.
Hearing this, the interrogator turns and signals the clerk to leave the room.
Now, there's just one other person in the room.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Let's talk about these documents, Lieutenant. What could possibly justify the sacrifice of so many soldiers to retrieve them?
He picks up the pen and waits.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Please maintain your candor, Lieutenant. Speak.
Bertolt takes a deep breath and resumes his account.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: My mission was to find and retrieve the descendants of an ancient arcanist family who were lost in the Central Asian region before the "Storm" arrived.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Was the source of this intel reliable?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I don't know, but my orders were clear. Maybe it was some kind of deal between the higher-ups and "them."

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Zeno's soldiers were deployed here as mercenaries, receiving compensation for their services.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Equipment, funds, personnel, access to local bases, and information about the arcanists.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: In the wake of the "Storm," we were under immense pressure to rebuild the arms academy. To secure resources, we had to do questionable things that ultimately tarnished our name.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Necessary evils. I understand. Go on.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: In 1964, the French conducted an excavation at the ruins of Ai-Khanoum in the north.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: It was an ancient Hellenistic city, lost under the sands of Inner Asia for nearly two thousand years.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Some of the artifacts were sent to Paris and some to the local museum. Then, war broke out.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: After the city was occupied, a batch of documents was secretly smuggled out and hidden in the mountains.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Since the spring of this year, our people have been discreetly searching for these documents. And finally, we have a lead on them.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Go on. What does this batch of documents contain?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Treasures of the Aegean Sea.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: A family tree, maps, diaries, archives, and epitaphs belonging to a family of Western arcanists who settled in Central Asia.
It is an incredible adventure, spanning thousands of miles and over the course of two millennia.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Their forebears rode with the Macedonian god-king as he conquered the known world. After the king's violent death, they shifted allegiances among several successors.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: When the one-eyed general triumphed in Gabiene, these fickle and war-loving veterans became part of his forces.
A volatile, unpredictable army. No wise man would ever grasp that blade without a hilt.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: After that, the arcanists within the army were sent east with their old comrades, gradually fading into the mountains and the annals of history.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: But they did not disappear. These bellicose descendants of arcanists later merged with the rising Sogdian tribes, and continued to thrive along the desert trade routes for centuries.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Chasing their ancestors' shadows, they stumbled upon the ancient city of Ai-Khanoum and set up a small arcanist commune nearby. But as fate would have it, the early century's penchant for war scattered them once more.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: My mission was to track down and bring back the descendants of this tribe, with these documents serving as vital clues.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Zeno needs these arcanists.
The officer takes several gulps of hot water, seemingly anxious about revealing the truth.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Have you told Lilya about all this?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Yes, she's in the loop, as I told you earlier.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Okay. I see.
The interrogator presses a button under the table and the clerk steps back into the room, resuming her place.

items.speaker: Interrogator III
items.text: Continue, Lieutenant. What happened next?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Are we really risking so many lives just for a few measly cottontails?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Eight hundred thousand lives were once sacrificed for just ten kilometers of land.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Though that's not quite the right comparison. That was a foolish battle.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Sacrifice is necessary if the result is worth it, little falcon.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Are you willing to sacrifice yourself?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I am.
The officer pulls out his gun without hesitation, prepared for what he knows is coming.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: What do you want me to do now?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Just understand the priorities of our mission, and never forget them.
Lilya clenches her fists and spits on the floor.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Yes, sir.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I understand your frustration, but a mission is a mission, and orders are still orders.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Besides, we need to think about what to do next. We have a lot of wounded to take care of.
Just then, Aleksei bursts through the door, eyeing the two from a distance.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Sir! You're bleeding! And what's with the gun?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I fell. It was nothing.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Yeah. Fell onto my fist.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Uh, what?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Don't worry about it. What's the matter, Aleksei?
He tucks his gun into his coat and wipes the blood from his lip.

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Earlier, Hassan mentioned herbs in these mountains that can stop bleeding. Maybe I can go find some.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: It's too dangerous to go alone. Besides, you don't know the lay of the land.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I can come.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: What are you all talking about? Let old Hassan in on it, eh?

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: Hassan should know the way.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Way? What way? I'm not catching your drift.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Aleksei and I are thinking of fetching some herbs. We're running low on medicine.

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Hmm, that could work.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You know these mountains well?

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Like the back of my hand! I was scampering about these slopes before I could even talk!

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: That settles it! Let the three of us give it a try, sir!
The officer hesitates.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Having more helping hands would've certainly made things easier, but the war and the "Storm" have cost us dearly.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I had planned to wait for reinforcements before moving out, but time was ticking, and dusk was closing in.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Spending the night there was out of the question, so I gave these brave soldiers the permission to go.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Alright, you have two hours.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Get back before the sun sets behind that mountain, or you're on your own.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: How are the wounded, Aleksei?

items.speaker: Aleksei
items.text: We've done all we can. I gave the last of the medicine to the others, and now I have an empty box that can hold a lot.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: What are we waiting for? Time's a-wasting, fellas!

items.speaker: Hassan
items.text: Just the three of us, ready to take on the world! Stay tuned for our epic success, haha!

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Bring your radar, Lilya. And if you happen to come across our lost comrades along the way, retrieve them.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You got it!

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: They set off, and I was left there to wait. To wait for reinforcements, for their return, or perhaps for the enemy's vengeance.
He calmly lowers his head and pauses for a moment.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Before long, I went looking for them. As soon as I heard gunshots on the road, I followed the sound with our men, but it was too late.
TO BE CONTINUED…
